title: 考研英语（旧）2006年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: In spite of "endless talk of difference," American society is an amazing machine for homogenizing people.
sentences.translation: 尽管存在"无休止的差异讨论"，美国社会却是一台令人惊叹的同质化机器。存在着"服饰和话语的民主化统一性，以及大众文化特有的随意性和缺乏恭敬"。人们被吸收进"消费文化"之中，这种文化由19世纪的百货商店开创，它们"在优雅的氛围中提供大量商品。这些商店不再是迎合知识精英的私密小店"，而是"任何人都可以进入的商店，无论其阶级或背景如何。这使购物变成了一种公共的、民主的行为"。大众媒体、广告和体育运动是推动同质化的其他力量。

sentences.text: There is "the democratizing uniformity of dress and discourse, and the casualness and absence of deference" characteristic of popular culture.
People are absorbed into "a culture of consumption" launched by the 19th-century department stores that offered "vast arrays of goods in an elegant atmosphere.
Instead of intimate shops catering to a knowledgeable elite," these were stores "anyone could enter, regardless of class or background.
This turned shopping into a public and democratic act."
The mass media, advertising and sports are other forces for homogenization.
Foreign-born Asians and Hispanics "have higher rates of intermarriage than do U.S.-born whites and blacks."
sentences.translation: 外国出生的亚裔和西班牙裔"异族通婚率高于美国本土出生的白人和黑人"。到第三代，三分之一的西班牙裔女性嫁给非西班牙裔，41%的亚裔美国女性嫁给非亚裔。

sentences.text: By the third generation, one third of Hispanic women are married to non-Hispanics, and 41 percent of Asian-American women are married to non-Asians.
The townsfolk don't see it this way and the local council does not contribute directly to the subsidy of the Royal Shakespeare Company.
sentences.translation: 镇上居民不这么看,当地议会也不直接向皇家莎士比亚剧团提供补贴。斯特拉特福德历来哭穷。然而,镇上的每家酒店似乎都在增建新的侧楼或鸡尾酒休息室。希尔顿酒店正在那里建造自己的酒店,你可以肯定它会装饰有哈姆雷特汉堡吧、李尔休息室、班柯宴会厅等等,而且价格会非常昂贵。

sentences.text: Stratford cries poor traditionally.
Nevertheless every hotel in town seems to be adding a new wing or cocktail lounge.
Hilton is building its own hotel there, which you may be sure will be decorated with Hamlet Hamburger Bars, the Lear Lounge, the Banquo Banqueting Room, and so forth, and will be very expensive.
When prehistoric man arrived in new parts of the world, something strange happened to the large animals: they suddenly became extinct.
sentences.translation: 当史前人类到达世界的新地区时,大型动物身上发生了一些奇怪的事情:它们突然灭绝了。较小的物种存活了下来。那些大型、生长缓慢的动物是容易捕获的猎物,很快就被猎杀至灭绝。现在,类似的事情可能正在海洋中发生。

sentences.text: Smaller species survived.
The large, slow-growing animals were easy game, and were quickly hunted to extinction.
Now something similar could be happening in the oceans.
Many things make people think artists are weird.
sentences.translation: 许多事情让人们认为艺术家很古怪。但最古怪的可能是这一点:艺术家的唯一工作就是探索情感,然而他们却选择专注于那些让人感觉糟糕的情感。

sentences.text: But the weirdest may be this: artists' only job is to explore emotions, and yet they choose to focus on the ones that feel bad.
This wasn't always so.
sentences.translation: 情况并非一直如此。最早的艺术形式,如绘画和音乐,是最适合表达快乐的。但从19世纪某个时候开始,越来越多的艺术家开始将幸福视为无意义的、虚假的,或者最糟糕的是无聊的,我们从华兹华斯的水仙花走向了波德莱尔的恶之花。

sentences.text: The earliest forms of art, like painting and music, are those best suited for expressing joy.
But somewhere from the 19th century onward, more artists began seeing happiness as meaningless, phony or, worst of all, boring, as we went from Wordsworth's daffodils to Baudelaire's flowers of evil.
You could argue that art became more skeptical of happiness because modern times have seen so much misery.
sentences.translation: 你可以说艺术变得对幸福更加怀疑,是因为现代社会经历了如此多的苦难。但这并不意味着早期时代不知道永无休止的战争、灾难和对无辜者的屠杀。事实上,原因可能恰恰相反:当今世界有太多该死的幸福了。

sentences.text: But it's not as if earlier times didn't know perpetual war, disaster and the massacre of innocents.
The reason, in fact, may be just the opposite: there is too much damn happiness in the world today.
People in earlier eras were surrounded by reminders of misery.
sentences.translation: 早期时代的人们被苦难的提醒所包围。他们工作到精疲力竭,生活几乎没有保障,英年早逝。在西方,在大众传播和识字普及之前,最强大的大众媒介是教会,它提醒信徒他们的灵魂处于危险之中,总有一天会成为蛆虫的食物。考虑到这一切,他们确实不需要他们的艺术也令人沮丧。

sentences.text: They worked until exhausted, lived with few protections and died young.

In the West, before mass communication and literacy, the most powerful mass medium was the church, which reminded worshippers that their souls were in danger and that they would someday be meat for worms.
Given all this, they did not exactly need their art to be a bummer too.
